name: International Protection (asylum, subsidiary, and national humanitarian protection)

qualifying_event.description: Refugee status requires a well-founded fear of persecution under the 1951 Refugee Convention; subsidiary protection applies where those criteria are not met but there is a real risk of serious harm if returned. A separate, narrower national 'humanitarian protection' status exists for cases outside both categories.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Evidence supporting the persecution/serious-harm claim, assessed by Cyprus's Asylum Service.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires meeting the criteria for refugee status or subsidiary protection, assessed by Cyprus's Asylum Service under the EU Common European Asylum System framework.
A narrower, national (non-EU-directive) protection status for cases falling outside refugee/subsidiary-protection criteria, granted at the authorities' discretion.

outcome.duration_length: national humanitarian protection: 12-month special residence permit (renewal options unclear); refugee/subsidiary protection permit durations not confirmed in sources reviewed

sources.title: Asylum Information Database (AIDA), European Council on Refugees and Exiles -- Cyprus country report
AIDA -- Cyprus: National protection statuses and return procedure

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Cyprus's initial build. Cyprus has a real, EU Common European Asylum System-compliant domestic protection framework (unlike Barbados/Dominica's 'never existed' cases) -- it is also, as an EU external-border state, one of the highest per-capita asylum-application recipients in the EU, making this a materially real route rather than a formality. STATUS SET TO DRAFT: sourced only via AIDA (a well-regarded NGO/civil-society legal-monitoring database, tier 3 per this dataset's convention, not a Cyprus government source) since gov.cy and the Cyprus Asylum Service's own pages were not reached in this pass. HONEST GAP: standard refugee/subsidiary-protection residence-permit durations were not confirmed in the sources fetched -- only the narrower 'national humanitarian protection' status's 12-month permit was; work_rights and study_rights set to 'restricted' as conservative defaults reflecting the source's description of discretionary, Labour-Department-gated employment authorisation, not a confirmed blanket restriction level for every protection type. pr_after_months (60) is an inferred figure (protection-holder residence feeding cy_long_term_residence's 5-year test) rather than one stated specifically for asylum in these sources.
